summary: Feed s124_double to 10 Gbps NDR is degraded: 99.2% of bytes are encrypted (exceeds 90% tolerance) and microbursts peak at 29.95 Gbps (299% of port capacity). NDR is blind to payload and dropping due to overload, severely reducing detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Almost all traffic (99.22%) is TLS/encrypted and is being forwarded to the NDR without prior decryption. No SSL visibility appliance or packet broker decryption is in path before the tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires full payload for detection but cannot inspect encrypted payloads; with 99% encrypted, signatures, JA3, and payload analytics are ineffective and threats inside TLS are missed.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt relevant TLS once at visibility layer and forward cleartext to NDR (with policy to respect privacy) to bring encrypted share below 90% and restore payload inspection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering aggregated/bursty traffic without load balancing. A 1ms microburst hit 29.95 Gbps vs the NDR's 10 Gbps port (299% of capacity), indicating sustained rate exceeds single tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR NIC buffer overrun and packet drops during bursts; incomplete flows, missed detections, and degraded NDR analytics despite no broker drops detected.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 3-4x 10G NDR ports/instances with flow-aware hashing to keep per-port utilization <80% and absorb 30 Gbps microbursts without loss.
